notes: Source text defect: the cardiac index threshold is missing in the downloaded NCD ('have a Cardiac Index (CI)' with no value), and as rendered it is unclear whether the OMM 45/60-day and IABP sub-bullets apply to inotrope-dependent patients. All LVAD cases therefore describe inotrope-dependent patients who also meet the OMM or IABP branch, and no case relies on cardiac index. Whether the team and credentialing requirements apply to post-cardiotomy VADs is also unclear; the post-cardiotomy case satisfies them. Section D (RV/BiV support, age < 18, congenital disease, acute HF without chronic HF) is left to MACs and is not tested.

criteria.text: LVAD is FDA approved for short-term or long-term mechanical circulatory support
criteria.span: Left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) are covered if they are FDA approved for short-term (e.g., bridge-to-recovery and bridge-to-transplant) or long-term (e.g., destination therapy) mechanical circulatory support for heart failure patients
Have New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class IV heart failure
Have a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 25%

criteria.text: OMM for >= 45 of last 60 days and failing, or advanced HF >= 14 days with IABP/temporary MCS dependence >= 7 days
criteria.span: Are on optimal medical management (OMM), based on current heart failure practice guidelines for at least 45 out of the last 60 days and are failing to respond

criteria.text: Team surgeon has implanted >= 10 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months with activity in the last year
criteria.span: At least one physician with cardiothoracic surgery privileges and individual experience implanting at least 10 durable, intracorporeal, left ventricular assist devices over the course of the previous 36 months with activity in the last year.

criteria.text: Facility-based multidisciplinary team incl. advanced HF cardiologist, VAD coordinator, social worker, palliative care specialist
criteria.span: The team members must be based at the facility and must include individuals with experience working with patients before and after placement of a VAD.

criteria.text: Facility credentialed by a CMS-approved organization
criteria.span: Facilities must be credentialed by an organization approved by CMS.

criteria.text: Post-cardiotomy VAD FDA approved for that purpose and used per labeling
criteria.span: VADs used for support of blood circulation post-cardiotomy are covered only if they have received approval from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for that purpose, and the VADs are used according to the FDA-approved labeling instructions.

cases.note: NYHA IV, LVEF 15%, inotrope dependent, OMM 58/60 days failing; full team, credentialed facility.
cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy, NYHA class IV symptoms, and LVEF 15% by echocardiography. He has been on guideline-based optimal medical management for 58 of the last 60 days without response and is dependent on continuous milrinone after two failed weaning attempts. He is not a transplant candidate. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.

cases.note: Post-cardiotomy indication: device FDA approved for post-cardiotomy support per labeling. LVEF 35% and NYHA criteria apply to the LVAD heart failure indication, not this one.
